title: Minimum-Length Path Visiting All Nodes

notes: The graph is connected and undirected, so every node can be reached from every other node.
constraints: If graph[a] contains b, then graph[b] contains a.
The input graph is always connected.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]
content.problemStatement:
You have an undirected, connected graph of `n` nodes labeled from `0` to `n - 1`. You receive an array `graph` where `graph[i]` is a list of all the nodes connected with node `i` by an edge.

Output *the length of the shortest path that visits every node*. You may start and stop at any node, you may revisit nodes multiple times, and you may reuse edges.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/05/12/shortest1-graph.jpg)

```
Input: graph = [[1,2,3],[0],[0],[0]]
Output: 4
Explanation: One possible path is [1,0,2,0,3]
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/05/12/shortest2-graph.jpg)

```
Input: graph = [[1],[0,2,4],[1,3,4],[2],[1,2]]
Output: 4
Explanation: One possible path is [0,1,4,2,3]
```

**Constraints:**

* `n == graph.length`
* `1 <= n <= 12`
* `0 <= graph[i].length < n`
* `graph[i]` does not contain `i`.
* If `graph[a]` includes `b`, then `graph[b]` includes `a`.
* The input graph is always connected.

notes: Because all edges have unit cost, BFS guarantees the first full-mask state is optimal.
Starting from all nodes simultaneously removes the need to try each starting node separately.
A state is revisited only once for each (mask, node) pair.
solution.approach: Use multi-source BFS on states (currentNode, visitedMask). The bitmask records which nodes have been visited. Start from every node with its single-node mask at distance 0, then expand level by level. The first state whose mask contains every node gives the shortest path length.

better.complexity: O(2^n * (n + m)) time and O(n * 2^n) space.
better.description: Represent each partial walk by its current node and visited-node mask, and search these states with BFS. This deduplicates walks that reach the same state, avoiding repeated work.

optimal.complexity: O(2^n * (n + m)) time and O(n * 2^n) space.
optimal.description: Use a multi-source BFS over (node, mask) states. Initialize one state for every possible starting node. For each edge, update the mask with the neighbor and enqueue unseen states. Stop when the mask equals (1 << n) - 1.

bruteForce.complexity: Exponential time; O(n) recursion depth for a depth-first implementation.
bruteForce.description: Enumerate possible walks from every starting node until all nodes have been visited. This quickly becomes exponential because many different walks and revisits are possible.

solution.timeComplexity: O(2^n * (n + m)), where m is the number of edges.

followUps: Why is ordinary BFS on graph nodes alone insufficient for this problem?
